desc: Shift attention within one frame without cutting.
verdict: RENDERED 2026-08-04. THIS MOVE DOES NOTHING at the post tier: no branch in fx_chain(), MAD against static exactly 0.00. Asked of the video model, LTX does not shift focus - it HALLUCINATES A HANGING CHAIN into the centre of frame and holds it there for the rest of the clip. Activity is 0.61, BELOW the 1.02 static floor, because the invented foreground is soft and lowers frame-to-frame high-frequency change. A textbook instance of the house rule: asked for an optical quality, the model rendered a noun instead. See rack_focus_prompted.mp4.
why_not: Needs to know which pixels are near and which are far. Nothing in the post chain knows that. A radial or vertical blur gradient would LOOK like a focus pull on a wide shot and be wrong on every close-up, which is the same lie in a softer filter.
needs: A depth ORDERING - not a geometry, and no occlusions are opened, so this is the cheapest of the three. Fixed-sigma gblur plus a time-ramped mask derived from depth, through maskedmerge. THE TRICK THAT MAKES IT WORK IN FFMPEG: gblur's sigma is not expression-evaluable, so ramp the MASK, not the blur strength. Verified to parse: [0:v]split[sharp][pre];[pre]gblur=sigma=12[blur];[1:v]format=gray,geq=lum=clip(255*min(1,abs((lum(X,Y)/255)-(T/DUR))/0.28),0,255)[mask];[sharp][blur][mask]maskedmerge
cost: The same per-beat depth pass dolly_zoom needs. Worth saying out loud: this is the one of the three that is a genuinely NEW expressive tool - shifting attention inside a frame without cutting is something this project cannot do at all today, and it costs one depth map and four filter nodes.
chain_verified: MEASURED 2026-08-04, CPU only, no GPU and no project file touched. The chain was run over a synthetic plate of three checkerboard bands with a synthetic depth map (left 255 = near, middle 128, right 0 = far), 48 frames at 24fps. IT DOES WHAT IT CLAIMS. Sharpness, as mean gradient magnitude per band: at t=0 far 58.01 / near 0.15; at t=end far 0.16 / near 59.10. A complete crossover, a ~390x ratio each way, and the midpoint frame is soft on BOTH outer bands because the plane of focus is passing through the middle one - which is what a focus pull looks like. Confirmed by eye on full-resolution crops, not only by the number. PROBE 2 could only say this chain PARSED; it now measures. What is still missing is the depth map, not the filter.
chain_params: sigma 12 = the out-of-focus strength; 0.28 = the depth-of-field band width; (T/DUR) = the focus plane sweeping 0->1 over the clip. Use (1-T/DUR) to pull the other way, or near+(far-near)*T/DUR to rack between two named planes instead of sweeping the whole range. Do NOT try to ramp gblur's sigma - it is not expression-evaluable. Ramping the MASK is what makes this work.
